rows.title: Combat on your phone
rows.body_md:
# Combat on your phone

When a fight is active the player UI switches to combat mode in place — you do not navigate away from the table.

## On your turn

1. You may use **one optional skill** (open DC roll), then **attack**, **cast**, or **use an item**.
2. Attack, cast, and item use each **end your turn**.
3. **End turn** passes without acting.

## Anytime

- Off-turn trained skill rolls where the scene allows them.
- **My HP** drawer for self-care — does not spend your turn.

## What you do not see

- Exact foe HP (health bands only).
- DM-only tactics and hidden mechanics.

## Morale and retreat

When foes break, the DM runs morale in the app. **Retreat** uses the house table — your phone may prompt for a party vote on how you flee.

## Dying

At 0 HP you are **dying** until stabilized or healed. First aid is a trained check with a fixed DC in the app.

_For the full phone surface, see the live app during session; this page is a reminder._

rows.title: Glossary
rows.body_md:
# Glossary

Short names for things you will see on the player app and in session.

## Crawler

Your PC on Floor Two — level, gear, deeds, and lore all hang off this identity.

## Deed

Something the table logged that counts toward achievements, sponsor taste, and evening scoring. You do not edit deeds on the wiki; they sync from play.

## Achievement wall

Trophy cards with hints. Progress shows on your phone first; the wiki exports **hints and tallies**, not the secret “for” text.

## Board bounty

A name from the **top ten** on the world leaderboard. Each session start the app rolls whether one of those names is “on the floor” tonight.

## Sponsor / booth

Evening brands that court crawlers based on deeds. Invites and contracts stay in the app until you earn them.

## Rival kitchen

An NPC your table turned into a Stadium opponent. Rivals reset when the evening resets.

## AI Favour

A once-per-roll token that counts as **advantage** on that check. You can hold at most one.

## Peek / live

**Peek** restores the world when the DM stops the app. **Live** play can diverge from the wiki snapshot at any time.

rows.title: House rules
rows.body_md:
# House rules

This table runs **Shadow Dark** with a few house conventions. The core rulebook is not republished here — bring your book or ask the DM for a PDF in the in-app Library at session.

**Auto-generated pages** (D20 rolls, party votes, phone combat, effect tables, etc.) are pulled from the app on each `wiki export` — scroll the Rules section in the handbook.

## Rolls at this table

- Stat and skill checks are usually a **flat d20** unless a status or untrained armour imposes disadvantage.
- Attacks use disadvantage when you are not proficient with the weapon you are swinging.
- Spellcasting checks and saves stay flat d20.

## The player app

- **Floor map** and **archive** only show what the party has already discovered in play.
- **Combat** on the phone is turn-gated; the server enforces what you can tap — greyed buttons are not a suggestion.
- **Party votes** (travel, rest, calling the night) need a majority of crawlers present.

## Floor Two flavour

- Achievements on the wall are **hints**, not full quest write-ups — reading between the lines is part of the game.
- Rivals at the Stadium are earned in play; this wiki only lists rivals your party has actually made.

_Edit this file, then run `uv run python -m dnd wiki export` to refresh the public site._

rows.title: Loot boxes
rows.body_md:
# Loot boxes

Achievement payouts and some scenes award **bronze**, **silver**, or **gold** boxes. Opening a box rolls on the tier’s table in the adventure data — the wiki does not publish the full d100 lists (that would spoil the dungeon).

## Tiers (flavor)

- **Bronze** — Junk, scraps, and vending-machine surprises — still useful if you are clever.
- **Silver** — Better gear and potions from the silver table.
- **Gold** — Premium pulls — rare kit and strong potions.

## At the table

The player app shows what you rolled after the DM confirms the open. Exact items stay in your inventory and gear archive, not on this public site.

rows.title: Using the player app
rows.body_md:
# Using the player app

The **player UI** is the site you open on your phone during session (usually port **8767** over Tailscale). Voice chat is for talking only — rolls, combat, inventory, and room text all happen here.

This walkthrough matches the current layout: **bottom nav** (Explore · Info · Me · Settings) and **Info** fold-outs. Screenshots refresh when Pete runs `make wiki-guide` on the game machine.

## Log in and Explore

You pick your crawler at login. **Explore** is the default tab: sticky header (name, HP, pack, luck, tank, status) and the **Floor Feed** — shelved pins for characters, people, obstacles, and items in your room.

IMG|assets/guide/01-explore.png|Explore — header and Floor Feed

Tap the **🎲** beside your name for the ability grid when the table calls for a check.

IMG|assets/guide/02-abilities.png|Ability strip — tap to roll when the DM calls for it

Room prose opens from the reader (**⌄ Read** on long cards). The **🗺** chip opens the zone map for rooms you have visited.

## Info tab (fold-outs)

Tap **Info** (book icon) in the bottom nav. Folds stay shut until you open them; which folds are open is remembered on your device.

| Fold | What it is |
|------|------------|
| **Quests** | Active quests, leads, and earned achievements (hints only — payouts are automatic) |
| **Activity** | Tonight's log rows (expand inline) |
| **Shop** | Sponsor booth when the table has one |
| **Archive** | Per-crawler discoveries — rooms, NPCs, items, obstacles (undiscovered entries are not listed) |
| **Sponsors / Bounty hunters** | Floor board rows; cook-off sandbox opens from the Stadium foot when you are there |

IMG|assets/guide/05-archive.png|Archive inside Info

**Floor map** also lives under Info (or the explore **🗺** chip) — zone diagram with room numbers that match the table.

IMG|assets/guide/06-floor-map.png|Floor map

## Me and Settings

**Me** is your sheet: inventory grid, spells, class abilities, skills, achievements list, and profile edits.

**Settings** (⚙) holds theme, text size, motion, contrast, alert level, warning pop-ups, and **Log out**.

## Pack and inventory

The **pack** line in the header opens gear: equipped rig, pack list, give/drop when the rules allow. You cannot edit core sheet stats from the phone — HP and loot come from play.

IMG|assets/guide/04-inventory.png|Inventory sheet

## Moving: solo exits vs party votes

**Solo travel:** tap an exit on the Floor Feed shelf (optional stealth/storm/investigate toggles). Only **your** crawler moves; room text and the map marker follow you, not the DM focus room.

**Party votes:** rest, call it a night, retreat, surrender, and scout use the vote bar when someone proposes them — a majority of crawlers **present** carries the vote. Solo exit chips do **not** open the vote bar.

IMG|assets/guide/08-party.png|Party-related controls (votes when a proposal is open)

## Combat (quick reminder)

When a fight starts, the UI **stays on this app** and switches to combat mode: on your turn you may use one optional skill, then **attack**, **cast**, or **use an item** — each of those ends your turn. You see foe **health bands**, not exact HP. See the **Combat on your phone** rule card for the full turn order.

## What the phone is not

- Not a character editor — the DM sheet is authoritative.
- Not a spoiler browser — archive and map only show what you have earned in play.
- Not a substitute for the **Shadowdark DCC Wiki** between sessions; the wiki is a static snapshot (rules stubs, hints, party export). During the night, this app is live.

_Questions at the table? Ask the DM. Between sessions, check Rules here on the wiki or the handbook search._

rows.title: D20 rolls (house)
rows.body_md:
# D20 rolls at this table

These are **house implementations** baked into the app — not a copy of the Shadow Dark book.

When a d20 is flat and when it is rolled at disadvantage. The one place the rule lives.

The game prescribing a roll, or a crawler using something they have, is a flat d20.
A preset the phone offers on an item, obstacle, or NPC is that prescribed roll.
Status effects, darkness, cover, and similar swing the dice. Untrained **weapon**
attacks and untrained **armour** on active rolls still impose disadvantage.

| Roll                                   | Flat d20                  | Disadvantage                      |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Ability (stat) check, skill use        | always                    |                                   |
| Attack                                 | weapon skill held         | weapon skill not held             |
| Armour or shield worn                  | skill held                | skill not held: active rolls      |
| Spellcasting check                     | always                    |                                   |
| Saves                                  | always                    |                                   |
| Passive checks (notice, etc.)          | always                    |                                   |
| Preset action on an item, obstacle, NPC| always                    |                                   |

Advantage and disadvantage **stack**: each +1 adds another d20 kept high; each
−1 adds another d20 kept low (double disadvantage = three dice, keep lowest).
Opposing sources sum (one of each is a flat roll).

_Source: `roll_mode.py`._

rows.title: Advantage & disadvantage
rows.body_md:
# Advantage and disadvantage

Stacking advantage and disadvantage on d20 rolls.

Each +1 or −1 adds another d20 in that direction: net −2 is three dice, keep
lowest; net +2 is three dice, keep highest. Opposing sources sum (one of each
is a flat roll).

On the phone, **AI Favour** on a roll counts as advantage for that check.

You can hold at most **1** favour token at a time. Net swing is clamped to **±5** in the roller.

_Source: `swing.py`, `party/model.py`._

rows.title: Skills on actions
rows.body_md:
# Skills on actions

Ranked DCC-style skills — catalog + per-PC ranks from abilities YAML.

Every skill starts at level 0 when acquired. Growth is +1 at most per
session, never in the session the skill was acquired (``skills_since``).

When a scene action is tagged with a skill you **actually have**, you get **+2** on the roll, **plus your rank** in that skill (rank 0 when you first learn it). Ranks cap at **15**.

If the check is an **obstacle** or other world interaction, spending **AI Favour** on that roll also gives advantage.

Authored cooldown tags on skills: `none`, `1/fight`, `1/day`. A session that runs past midnight still counts as one night for growth (**12**-hour rollover).

_Source: `party/skills.py`, `skill_check.py`._

rows.title: Party votes
rows.body_md:
# Party votes

Only **one** party proposal is open at a time. A **majority of crawlers present** carries it — you do not wait for everyone to tap.

Kinds in the app: rest, end_night, retreat, surrender, scout.

| Kind | What it is for |
|------|----------------|
| `rest` | Camp / rest together |
| `end_night` | Call the night and reset evening-scoped state |
| `retreat` | Leave a fight (only during combat) |
| `surrender` | End the fight restrained at faction HQ |
| `scout` | Peek at a connected room (proposer runs the read) |

**Moving** is per crawler (Try sheet exit chips) — storm / sneak / search forms: **`storm`, `sneak`, `search`**.

Votes stay open about **30** seconds unless a majority passes sooner. Propose and vote from the **player app** vote bar when a proposal is open.

_Source: `party_vote.py`, `pc_travel.py`, `party_moves.py`._

rows.title: Rest & camp
rows.body_md:
# Rest and camp

Rest: heal, clear conditions, refill pools — and whether the night was quiet.

Party **rest** (vote or DM) runs a full recovery pass:

- Heal **Xd6** where **X** is your level (minimum 1).
- Clear up to **CON mod** condition units (minimum **1**); afflictions left-to-right unless you pick.
- Refill mana and clear per-rest ability uses.

Then a **d6** decides how quiet the night was (`roll_rest_interruption`):

| d6 | Band | What it means |
|----|------|----------------|
| 1–2 | encounter | Hostile interruption — table runs the fight; CON **DC 12** saves per PC are surfaced as text, not auto-rolled |
| 3–4 | omen | Flavour omen only |
| 5–6 | clean | Everyone wakes **Bolstered** (+ temp HP, about an hour) |

_Source: `party/rest.py`._

rows.title: Down at 0 HP
rows.body_md:
# Down at 0 HP

Down and dying: the death timer and the turn-start d20.

A PC at 0 HP keeps a seat but does not act. Dropping starts a death timer of
``d4 + CON mod`` (minimum 1). Each time their seat comes up they roll a d20:
a natural 20 stands them up at 1 HP to take that turn; a natural 1 is death;
other rolls tick the timer down, and when it hits 0 they go **stable** (out
cold at 0 HP) instead of dying automatically. Healed to 1+ HP by anyone, the
timer simply stops.

**First aid** (when the table allows it) uses a check against **DC 17** to stop the death clock and bring someone to **1 HP**.

_Source: `combat/dying.py`._

rows.title: Fleeing combat
rows.body_md:
# Fleeing a fight

When a **retreat** vote passes, combat ends and the app rolls the house **d10 retreat table** **2** times (panic on a 9 can chain).

| d10 | Result | Effect |
|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | Stumble | A crawler takes 1d4 damage. |
| 2 | Dropped gear | Something falls on the floor here. |
| 3 | Spilled coin | A crawler loses 1d10 sp. |
| 4 | Torn pack | Another item hits the dirt. |
| 5 | Spilled purse | A crawler loses 2d10 sp. |
| 6 | Shaken | Someone is Distracted fleeing. |
| 7 | Prone | Someone lands wrong — Prone. |
| 8 | Lost supplies | Something from a pack is left behind. |
| 9 | Panic | Roll the table one more time. |
| 10 | Clean break | No extra cost this roll. |

**Surrender** (party vote during combat) ends the fight with **no d10 retreat table**; everyone is **Restrained** and the table moves to the hostile faction's HQ room when the data has one.

**Personal flee** applies one d10 retreat penalty to the fleeing crawler only; the fight continues for everyone else.

_Source: `combat/retreat.py`, `retreat_flee.py`, `combat_surrender.py`._

rows.title: Combat house rules
rows.body_md:
# Combat — house rules in the app

These are enforced by the combat engine and phone API, not optional table chatter.

## Distance

Combat uses **Close / Near / Far** lanes (close → near → far). Default PCs start **near**; hostiles usually **close**. Weapon reach is **melee**, **thrown** (near), or **ranged** (far).

## Round clock

**3** rounds are the “free” fight before the DM is nudged to call an outcome — nothing hard-stops the fight after that.

## Crits and fumbles

- **PC nat 20:** max the weapon damage dice, then roll them again once (not doubled dice).
- **Monster nat 20:** double the number of damage dice.
- **Nat 1 on attack:** automatic DEX check vs **DC 12** (fumble).

## Morale

Foe morale: one check when the hostile side is down to half its hit points.

The pool is every hostile's max HP this fight, the fallen included, so one
rule covers both shapes of fight — a lone boss checks at half its HP, a swarm
of one-HP goblins checks when half of them are down, and a boss with minions
weighs mostly on the boss. Checked once a fight: the strongest hostile
(highest to-hit, then biggest) rolls d20 + to-hit against DC 12. A fail
breaks them; the DM picks pursue (fight on) or let them flee.

Morale DC in code: **12**.

## Backstab

Thieves (classes: thief) and ledger talents get **+2** weapon dice on a **round-one** swing against a foe that has **not acted yet** and acts after you in initiative.

## Mana

Max mana = **2 + INT mod**, never below 0. Full rest refills to cap.

_Source: `combat/dice.py`, `combat/morale.py`, `combat/models.py`, `combat/rails.py`, `combat/backstab.py`, `party/crawler.py`._

The pool is every hostile's max HP this fight, the fallen included, so one rule covers both shapes of fight — a lone boss checks at half its HP, a swarm of one-HP goblins checks when half of them are down, and a boss with minions weighs mostly on the boss. Checked once a fight: the strongest hostile (highest to-hit, then biggest) rolls d20 + to-hit against DC 12. A fail breaks them; the DM picks pursue (fight on) or let them flee.

Morale DC in code: 12.

Backstab

Thieves (classes: thief) and ledger talents get +2 weapon dice on a round-one swing against a foe that has not acted yet and acts after you in initiative.

Mana

Max mana = 2 + INT mod, never below 0. Full rest refills to cap.

# Combat on the phone

When a fight is active the player UI switches **in place** — you are not leaving the handbook app for a different mode.

**On your turn:** you may use one optional **skill** roll, then **attack**, **cast**, or **use an item**. Attack, cast, and item use each **end your turn**. **End turn** passes without acting.

**What you do not see:** exact foe HP (bands only), DM tactics, hidden mechanics. Turn gating is enforced **server-side** — greyed buttons are not hints.

**Battle map:** you see miniature positions; full cover targets show **No shot** and cannot be selected.

# Achievements on the wall

Achievements a crawler has stumbled into: the first move pops the clue.

Nothing is listed up front. The first time a crawler's own deeds meet an
achievement's ``start`` — or, unauthored, a default read off its ``when`` —
their phone gets the ``hint`` as a clue, once. ``started`` in the achievement
ledger remembers who has heard, so the 4-second sweep never repeats itself.

rows.title: Floor Two conventions
rows.body_md:
# Floor Two — table conventions

Rival kitchens: who the party has made an enemy of, and who it cooks against next.

The loop is endless: hunt the jungle, cook at the Stadium, win into the Library,
back to the jungle. Each service draws one opponent. A rival is drawn at random
from the party's rivals (never the same one twice running when there's a
choice) with a score frozen from its authored range and whichever of its tricks
fire. No rivals at all and the party cooks the house show instead: a par that
rises every time they beat it.

The draw is announced before ingredients are committed and is held until the
service is submitted, so reopening the panel never rerolls it.

Everything here lasts one game night. A new evening (session start, or the
party calling it a night) means a new table: no rivals, the house par back to
its start, and only tonight's deeds can make new ones.

**Archive** on the phone lists rooms, people, and gear only after the party has **discovered** them in play — same boundary as this handbook's discovered sections.

rows.title: Effect tables
rows.body_md:
# Quick reference tables

These are the **in-game effect tables** the DM rolls from (injuries, potions, madness, etc.). 
Names and outcomes only — not Shadow Dark core rules.

## Sponsor buffs
### Sponsor buffs
- **Interface Sight** — You can see invisible and hidden creatures (tooltip outlines stay on).
- **Nine Takes** — The next nine times you go to 0 HP, regain 1 HP — the AI keeps resetting the stunt.
- **Fireproof Clause** — You are immune to damage from fire (sponsor liability waiver).
- **Set Rigging** — You can crawl on walls and sheer surfaces like a prop mount.
- **Deep-Floor Gill** — You can breathe water as though it were air — useful in flooded tutorial wings.
- **Mob Whisper** — You can speak to and understand animals and simple mobs long enough to negotiate.
- **Licensed Cast Eye** — Your casting eye sharpens for an hour — watermark in the corner of vision.
- **Kill Count Heal** — When you kill a creature, heal 1d6 hit points; audience cheer optional.
- _…and 4 more rows_

## Floor maladies
### Floor maladies
- **Gut Rot Canteen** — Stomach sloshes like a bad meal from Pam's line. Loud, humiliating noises. No surprise actions until treated.
- **Claim Mark Rash** — Shimmering bite marks bloom across the skin. Mobs with faction tags treat you as "already processed."
- **Influencer's Tongue** — You cannot stop exaggerating for the camera. Lies grow more ridiculous the longer you speak.
- **Countdown Fatigue** — Sudden drowsiness. When you rest, you dream of the public timer eating your name.
- **Implant Glow-Spots** — Pale spots pulse when achievements pop. Animals stare; janitor mobs seem… curious.
- **Sponsor Breath** — Every word smells of cheap cologne and regret. NPC reactions worsen unless bribed or charmed.
- **Itchwire** — Unbearable itching as if tiny hands keep poking you. Concentration is… optimistic while Followers climb.
- **Oathband Fungus** — A fungal band creeps around a finger or wrist and saps you until it is cut off.
- _…and 2 more rows_

## Contraband & sponsor samples
### Contraband & sponsor samples
- **Voidwalk Patch** — Walk through objects for 1 round, then confused for 10 minutes. A chyron reads PRODUCT PLACEMENT.
- **Foot Shock** — Your worst fears as interface pop-ups. Frightened 1 hour, then one prophetic glimpse the AI won't explain.
- **Implant Static** — Telepathy within near distance for 1 hour, then mute for 12 hours — the syndicate rebooted your voice slot.
- **Graveyard Shift Stim** — See in the dark for 4 hours, then blinded by bright light for a day (including achievement flashes).
- **Engagement Rush** — Advantage to notice things, disadvantage on INT checks for 1 hour (paranoia counts as content).
- **Blackout Step** — Twice within the hour, step from one shadow into another you can see. Then exhausted — the edit team adds bags under your eyes.
- **Broadcast Scream Ampule** — Once within the hour, a scream that makes all near creatures flee. Then voiceless for a day (subtitles only).
- **Crimson Sponsor Shot** — +2 STR for 1 hour, then 2d10 damage as it wears off. Side effects may include on-camera vomiting.
- _…and 12 more rows_

## Sponsor backlash
### Sponsor backlash
- **Forsaken** — Your sponsor pulls the plug. You can't make any Divine-keyword cast until you complete compliance.
- **Smitten** — Branded light lashes back on live feed. Take 1d8 radiant damage.
- **Wrong Script** — The cast comes out backwards, and the words will not come right for ten minutes.
- **Muted Mic** — Your voice is taken until your next rest. No casts, no speech; subtitles only.
- **Stigmata** — Your palms bleed. You are Bleeding until you pray on camera for an hour or sign a waiver.
- **Heretic's Mark** — A glowing product sigil brands your brow. Faithful NPCs and camera drones shun you until compliance.
- **Rival Whispers** — A rival network answers instead and will not stop whispering.
- **Relic Crack** — Your Divine trinket cracks, and you are off your game until it is mended.
- _…and 4 more rows_

## Broadcast injuries
### Broadcast injuries
- **Heart Attack** — Pass a DC 15 CON check or your heart seizes and you are paralyzed for three rounds.
- **Lop** — You lose a limb. Roll 1d4: 1. Leg, 2. Arm, 3. Foot, 4. Hand.
- **Blinded** — You lose an eye (DISADV on sight-based checks).
- **Torn Muscle** — You permanently lose 1 point of STR.
- **Severed Tendon** — You permanently lose 1 point of DEX.
- **Ruptured Spleen** — You permanently lose 1 point of CON.
- **Concussion** — You permanently lose 1 point of INT.
- **Ringing Ears** — You permanently lose 1 point of INT.
- _…and 12 more rows_

## Floor madness
### Floor madness
- **Off Air** — You retreat into your mind and lock up. The camera keeps rolling.
- **On-Mic Breakdown** — You scream, laugh, or weep into the mic until it passes.
- **Run** — Whatever set this off, you need to be far away from it.
- **Backwards Babble** — Only Syndicate Standard comes out, and it comes out backwards.
- **Rip and Tear** — The engagement quota is red. You have to make it green.
- **Previously On** — Recap footage bleeds into live vision. Half of what you see already happened.
- **Compliance Mode** — You obey any order that isn't obviously self-destructive. Sponsors love it.
- **Wrong Hunger** — You need to eat something wrong — dirt, slime, set fungi, a Pet Biscuit wrapper.
- _…and 12 more rows_

## Fungi
### Fungi
- **Bloodcap** — Violently sick. Lose 1d6 HP and your next turn.
- **Hot Mic Horns** — Burning mouth. You can only whisper for a day.
- **Marshguts** — Your stomach churns for 1 hour. Disadvantage on everything.
- **Grinning Jenny** — You can't stop smiling or laughing for 1 hour.
- **Lambent Stinkhorn** — You reek for a day. Nothing is surprised by you.
- **Numblings** — Your limbs go numb. Half speed for 1 hour, but you ignore the next 1d6 damage.
- **Mottlecap** — Your skin turns purple with yellow splotches for 1d4 days.
- **Break-Room Cluck** — You cluck like a chicken for 1 hour, and chickens understand you.
- _…and 12 more rows_

## Floor contamination
### Floor contamination
- **Rasping** — Your vocal cords warp. You can only speak in a halting gurgle.
- **Rotting** — Your lips, nose and ears blacken and wither.
- **Molting** — Blisters and multicoloured lesions burst and peel, exposing the raw sinew underneath.
- **Lambent Glow** — You emit a dim octarine glow.
- **Ocular Tumors** — Eyeballs open somewhere on your body. They blink out of sync.
- **Adonis** — You morph into someone more beautiful. Slightly too beautiful.
- **Aquatic Adaptation** — Fins and gills. You can breathe underwater and swim as fast as you walk.
- **Amorphous Form** — Your bones and organs go gelatinous. You fit through a six-inch gap.
- _…and 12 more rows_

## Unlabeled vials
### Unlabeled vials
- **Blindness** — Your eyes film over white. Blinded for 1 hour.
- **Confusion** — You act at random for 1d4 rounds.
- **Fear** — You flee the nearest creature for 1d4 rounds.
- **Enfeeblement** — Disadvantage on STR checks and attacks for 1 hour.
- **Slow** — You move and act at half speed for 10 rounds.
- **Wrong Form** — At the next prime-time stinger — or the next big achievement flash — you become a wolf. Only a cure can stop it.
- **Age** — You age 1d10 years in a heartbeat, and your bones know it.
- **Alter Voice** — Your voice becomes someone else's for a day.
- _…and 12 more rows_

## Cast glitch
### Cast glitch
- **Devastation** — Roll twice more and both results land.
- **Backfire** — The spell backfires and hurts you.
- **Hand Slipped** — Your hand slips; the cast goes wide and you lose your footing.
- **Mind Wound** — You can't use this ability again for a week — cooldown locked by the AI.
- **Discorporation** — One random piece of your gear vanishes forever (inventory sync error).
- **Cast Worm** — Each turn you lose a random ability until you pass a DC 12 CON check.
- **Energy Surge** — You glow bright purple for 10 rounds; enemies have advantage to hit you.
- **The Horror** — You scream in garbled Syndicate Standard for 3 rounds, drawing everything nearby.
- _…and 12 more rows_

_Source: `dungeons/global/effects.yaml`._

rows.title: Classes
rows.body_md:
# Classes

Level 1 picks your class for life. HP is the class hit die plus CON.

## Arms Manufacturer

You build the weapon the room is about to regret.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Workshop — once per rest. Turn salvage into one weapon, or add +1 to hit or +1 damage to a weapon you have. It comes with one quirk. You learn the quirk the first time you use it.
- **Major** Ordnance — once per scene. Throw or plant a device you built: 2d6 damage, near, DEX check for half.
- **Minor** Appraise — you know a weapon's damage, quirks, and price without a roll.

## Baba Yaga

The hut still comes when called. The dog is late.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Hut — once per floor. Call the hut. It is a safe room for one rest, then it walks off.
- **Major** Hex — once per scene. One near foe has disadvantage on its next attack. A CHA check ends the hex before then.
- **Major** Iron teeth — your bite is 1d6. Once per scene, eat a fallen foe's heart and heal 1d6.

## Banana Farmer

A seed, a tree, a ration, and a peel under the next foot.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Seed shot — at will. Near attack from your palm, 1d8, using INT.
- **Major** Rapid grove — once per scene. Grow a tree: full cover, climbable, and one ration of bananas.
- **Minor** Peel — scatter peels, near. A foe that crosses them makes a DEX check or falls prone. Once per scene.

## Basement Alchemist

A heal, a cloud, and a hole in someone's armour. Mixed in a bucket.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Brew — once per rest. One potion: heal 1d6, +2 AC for one scene, or ignore fire, cold, or poison for one scene.
- **Major** Acid flask — at will. Thrown, near, 1d6. That target's AC is 1 lower until the acid is cleaned off.
- **Major** Fumes — once per scene. Near foes make a CON check or have disadvantage on their next attack.

## Bike Messenger

Gone before the swing lands. You still know the way back.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Wheels — while you are on the bike, you move double. A foe on foot catches you only by winning a DEX check.
- **Major** Dodge — once per round, on the bike, when you are hit: DEX check, take half damage.
- **Minor** Courier — you know the fastest route through anywhere you have already mapped.

## Biker Knight from Mars - Pennsylvania

A knight's oath, and a chopper that answers to it.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Chopper — a charge on the bike deals +1 damage die. The bike has 8 HP. At 0 HP you are on foot until a rest. (+1 dmg_dice, when charge)
- **Major** Oath — +1 AC while an ally beside you is hurt. Advantage on checks against fear. (+1 ac, when guarding)

## Boring Ol' Warlock

Your sponsor answers. The blast is the boring part.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Patron's blast — at will. Far spell attack, 1d10, using CHA.
- **Major** Bad Faith — when a sponsor price, a deal, or a punishment hurts you, you heal half of that damage. Name one damage type your patron resists. You resist it too.
- **Minor** Sponsor line — once per floor, your patron answers one yes-or-no question.

## Capoeira Practitioner

Move, and the circle has trouble hitting you. Stop, and the kick lands.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Ginga — +1 AC on any turn you moved. (+1 ac, when moved)
- **Major** Kick flow — unarmed kicks deal 1d8 and can shove the target one step.

## Caretake Array Chassis

A Chip medic. The stencil is missing a letter. The beam is not.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Repair beam — heal one ally near you for 1d6 + your INT modifier. Twice per rest.
- **Major** Triage scan — you see every ally's HP and conditions.
- **Major** Stabilise — once per scene, touch a dying crawler. They wake at 1 HP.

## Chuuni Brooding Edgelord

Name the curse, stack it, and drink what comes off.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Affliction — a foe takes 1 damage at the start of each of its turns. Cast it again on the same foe to add a stack, up to 2.
- **Major** Life drain — at will. Near spell attack, 1d6, using INT. You heal half the damage (round down).
- **Major** Shadow — a shadow scouts for you and gives you advantage on stealth.

## Concierge Protocol Chassis

The floor thinks you work here. Keep your hands off the exhibits.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Recurring NPC — locals and non-boss mobs treat you as dungeon staff until you attack or steal.
- **Major** Service voice — once per scene. CHA check to get one reasonable favour from a non-hostile NPC.
- **Minor** Itinerary — your chassis points to the nearest safe room, and to any stairs the party has already seen.

## Conference Loot Goblin

A badge, a favour, and a tote bag. The swing is someone else's job.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Contacts — once per floor, you know one useful person here who owes you a small favour.
- **Major** Borrowed access — once per floor, your badge opens one locked door or staff room. Boss doors stay shut.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Breakdown — once per scene. Each near foe attacks you this round, or takes 1d4. A CHA check ignores it.
- **Major** Inked hide — +1 AC. You breathe water and swim at full speed. (+1 ac)

## Disgruntled Chef

Dinner is a buff. The knife is sharper than your patience.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Mise en place — once per rest, cook. Each crawler who eats picks one: +1 to hit for the next fight, 2 temporary HP, or advantage on one check.
- **Major** Kitchen arsenal — knives and cleavers deal +1 damage. A thrown pan stuns on a natural 20. (+1 dmg, when knife or cleaver)
- **Minor** Taste test — you know poison, potion, or rot by tasting it.

## Dreamwalker Assassin

Set the nightmare. Then hit whatever fell into it.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Nightmare trap — once per scene, set one trap in a near space. The first foe to enter it loses its next action.
- **Major** Dream strike — your attacks deal +1 damage die to a foe that is frightened or asleep.
- **Major** Sleepwalk — once per scene. One non-boss foe of your level or lower falls asleep. INT check.

## Exotic Dancer

One foe forgets its turn. The camera does not.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Spotlight — once per scene. One foe that can see you loses its next action. CHA check. On a success, gain 1 Popularity.
- **Major** Camera work — +1 to hit while a camera drone has you in frame. (+1 atk, when on camera)
- **Minor** Pole work — climb or swing over an obstacle without a check.

## Galactic Luchador

Grab them, name the move, make the cheap seats care.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Grapple — advantage to grab. On your turn, a held foe takes 1d6, or you slam it for 2d6 and the grab ends.
- **Major** Taunt — once per scene, instead of moving: +1 damage for the rest of the scene, and 1 Popularity if they are watching. (+1 dmg, when taunted)

## Gladiator

More of them is a better show. The crowd pays for the extra swing.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Arena-born — +1 to hit while two or more foes are adjacent to you. (+1 atk, when outnumbered)
- **Major** Intimidate — once per scene. One non-boss foe of your level or lower flees or kneels. CHA check.

## Grease Monkey

A wrench, a thrown tool, and a machine that should have stayed broken.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Wrench — wrenches deal 1d8. A hit can disable a machine or a trap until it is fixed.
- **Major** Thrown tools — you may throw a tool instead of swinging: near, 1d6, and it returns to your belt.
- **Minor** Patch job — during a rest, you repair armour, a vehicle, or a Chip crawler.

## Gundamless Gundam Pilot

The training, the trauma, and a mech that has not shipped.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Pilot reflexes — you act first in the opening round of a fight.
- **Major** Newtype sense — once per scene, one attack against you has disadvantage.
- **Minor** Mech manual — you can operate a vehicle or a machine that is not a boss, without a check.

## Herculean Laborer

You push the room over, catch your breath, and do it again.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Overwhelming force — a melee hit pushes a foe one step. A foe smaller than you also falls prone.
- **Major** Monstrous stamina — heal 1d4 at the end of each fight.

One lecture. Then detention. The class is taking notes.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Lecture — once per scene. One foe that hears you has disadvantage on its next attack, and one ally who heard you gets +1 to hit that foe this round. INT check.
- **Major** Detention — once per fight, when an ally drops to 0 HP: +1 damage and advantage on STR checks until the fight ends. (+1 dmg, when raging)

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Jack of all trades — +1 on any check you have no skill for.
- **Major** Sample — once per scene, make a check as if you had a skill an adjacent ally has, at rank 0.
- **Minor** Hobby kit — name the tool this job needs. You are carrying one.

## Kintsukuroi

A killing blow leaves gold in the crack, and the crack hits back.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Golden Scar — once per fight, a blow that would drop you to 0 HP drops you to 1 instead. Mark one Golden Scar.
- **Major** Broken but whole — +1 damage per Golden Scar you earned this floor, up to +2. +1 AC while you are below half HP. (+1 ac, when below half HP)

## Kitsune

Fox or face, fire in the palm, and iron still hates you.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Fox shape — shift between fox and person freely. Your melee attacks use CHA instead of STR.
- **Major** Fox-fire — at will. Near spell attack, 1d6, using CHA. It lights the area. Iron weapons deal +1 damage to you.
- **Minor** Illusion — once per scene, one still image or one sound, no bigger than a person.

## Landsknecht

A ridiculous sword, and one ally who hits because you are standing there.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Doppelsöldner — two-handed weapons deal +1 damage. (+1 dmg, when two-handed)
- **Major** Battlefield presence — once per round, one ally near you gets +1 to hit.

## Librarian Archivist

See a spell once. Cast it later. File the weakness beside it.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Catalogue — when you see a spell cast, write it down, replacing the spell already in the book. Cast the written spell once per floor.
- **Major** Weakness index — once per scene, name one foe you can see. You learn one weakness. Allies deal +1 damage to it for the scene.
- **Major** Bind scrolls — once per rest, combine two scrolls into one page. Cast it once per rest.

## Library Militia

Shush the caster. Then hit whoever never heard you coming.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Shush — once per scene. One near foe makes an INT check or cannot cast or shout until your next turn.
- **Major** Stack patrol — advantage on your first attack against a foe that has not noticed you.
- **Minor** Top shelf — reach, climb, and grab what is far above you without a check.

## Mage Tank

A shield of runes, and a hammer that comes back.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Arcane shield — once per scene. The next hit on you or an adjacent ally is reduced by 1d6.
- **Major** Hammer throw — at will. Far, 1d8, and the hammer returns to your hand.

Eat the mob, learn it, and serve one piece of it tonight.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Taste — eat part of a slain mob. You learn one weakness, and you resist its damage type until the next floor.
- **Major** Monster cuisine — once per rest, cook one part into a dish. You gain one of that mob's abilities for the next scene.
- **Minor** Iron stomach — poison and rotten food do not harm you when you eat them.

## Ordinance Battery Chassis

The stencil is misspelled. The cannon is not.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Arm cannon — at will. Far, 1d8. It does not need to be reloaded.
- **Major** Hair trigger — once per scene, when a foe hits an ally near you, you take your turn immediately after that hit.

## Overcompensating Mechanic

A suit you built at home. It grants +2 AC until something important falls off.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Custom mech — entering the suit takes one round. While you are in it, +2 AC. The suit has 8 HP. At 0 it is junk until repaired. (+2 ac, when in mech)
- **Major** Hardpoint — one weapon mounted on the suit deals +1 damage die while you are in it. (+1 dmg_dice, when in mech)
- **Major** Field repair — once per rest, restore 1d6 HP to the suit, or 1d4 HP to an ally.

## Pack Alpha

One wolf, your call, and a bonus when you bite the same throat.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Pack call — one wolf (6 HP, 1d6 bite) fights with you and returns next floor.
- **Major** Shared lead — +1 to hit for you and the wolf when you both attack the same foe.
- **Minor** Howl — your wolf and your allies hear you anywhere on this floor.

## Pirate Captain

Point at an ally and they act. Point at a coward and they drop the gold.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Command — once per scene, one ally near you takes a move or an attack on your turn. You do not also attack.
- **Major** Dread reputation — once per scene. One non-boss foe of your level or lower surrenders or hands over what it is carrying. CHA check.
- **Minor** Treasure nose — you know whether the room you are in is hiding valuables.

## Samurai Retainer

The first cut is the deep one. A miss at you gets an answer.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Iaijutsu — your first attack each fight deals +1 damage die. (+1 dmg_dice, when first attack)
- **Major** Counter — once per scene, when a melee attack misses you, you strike back.

## Sluggernaut Chassis

Fists from a title fight, and a guard that makes them miss.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Iron fists — unarmed punches deal 1d8 and stun on a natural 20.
- **Major** Rope-a-dope — +1 AC against melee. When a melee attack misses you, your next punch has advantage. (+1 ac, when against melee)

## Soul Train Conductor

Dance the life out of one foe and into the crawler beside you.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Soul siphon — at will, as your attack. One foe near you takes 1d6. Once per scene, one ally near you also heals that amount.
- **Major** All aboard — once per scene, one fallen foe gets up as a dancer (6 HP, 1d6) until the scene ends.
- **Major** Groove — once per scene, allies who can hear you get +1 to hit until your next turn.

## Spartan Hoplite

Shield up. The lane behind you stays yours.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Shield wall — +1 AC. Each ally adjacent to you also has +1 AC. (+1 ac)
- **Major** Hold the line — you cannot be shoved or knocked down. Once per round, when a foe tries to move past you, you may attack that foe.

## Swiss Army Knight

A different weapon each turn, and each new one hits harder.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Generalist — +1 damage for each different weapon type that has hit this fight, up to +2.
- **Major** Quick swap — switch weapons for free on your turn.

## Symbiotic Slayer

You and your pet share eyes, then you share a target.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Mind meld — you see and hear through your pet. It acts on your turn, wherever it is.
- **Major** Hunt as one — when you and your pet both hit the same foe, each of you deals +1 damage.
- **Minor** Pet bond — your pet heals 1d4 whenever you rest.

## Televangelist

Temporary HP for the flock. A real heal when the camera is on.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Sermon — once per scene. Each ally who hears you gains 1d4 temporary HP.
- **Major** Laying on of hands — once per scene. Heal one ally 1d8. If a camera sees it, gain 1 Popularity.
- **Minor** Collection plate — once per floor, a crowd you preach to pays you 1d6 gold.

A far bolt, a trap switched off, and one die rolled again.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Execute — at will. Far spell attack, 1d8, using INT.
- **Major** Debug — once per scene. Cancel one spell, trap, or machine you can see. INT check.
- **Major** Patch — once per scene. Reroll one die you just watched. The new roll stands.

## Tsukumogami Smith

A fresh soul in a tool. A second soul starts to poison you.

- **Hit die** d4
- **Major** Soul-bind — put one fresh corpse's soul into an object. It gains one ability of the dead and can act (1d6, 4 HP). A second bound item poisons you: disadvantage on checks until you release one.
- **Major** Earth shape — once per scene. Reshape stone or earth near you into a wall, a pit, or cover.
- **Major** Kiln — once per rest. Move a bound soul into a new object, or repair one broken object.

## TV Bake Show Host

A rest, a bake, a +1, and a smile for the drone.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Showstopper bake — once per rest. Each ally who eats has +1 to hit for the next fight, and you gain 1 Popularity.
- **Major** Play to camera — once per scene. A stylish action gives you 1 Popularity and advantage on your next CHA check.
- **Minor** Soggy bottom — once per scene, insult a foe's work. It has disadvantage on its next attack.

## Underwater Basket Weaver

Learn it shallow, weave two skills into a third, and do not come up for air.

- **Hit die** d6
- **Major** Quick study — once per floor, after you see a skill used, you learn it at rank 0.
- **Major** Weave — name two skills you know. You gain a skill that applies when both would matter. Roll it at the lower rank. Name it in six words.
- **Minor** Hold breath — you can stay underwater ten times longer than a normal breath.

## Viking Raider

Rage, a worse AC, and something worth taking once they stop moving.

- **Hit die** d8
- **Major** Berserk — once per fight: +2 damage and advantage on attacks, and -2 AC, until the fight ends. (+2 dmg, -2 ac, when berserk)
- **Major** Pillage — after a fight, you find one extra mundane item in the wreck.

# Races

Race picks open at levels 2, 6, 9; a later pick swaps the old one.

## Angel

The halo is on. So is the camera.

- **Major** Radiant — bright light, near, until you put it out. +1 damage against undead and demons. (+1 CHA)
- **Minor** Glide — fall any distance. You take no damage.
- **Weakness** Halo — disadvantage on stealth. A foe in the dark attacks you before its allies. (-1 DEX)

## Ashen

Bark, and a grudge against every torch.

- **Major** Bark — DR 2. You cannot be Poisoned. (+2 CON, +2 dr)
- **Minor** Rooted — you need no food and no sleep.
- **Weakness** Tinder — fire damage against you is doubled. (-1 DEX)

## Cryak Draconian

Ruby scales, a short flight, and an oath you will regret on camera.

- **Major** Ruby scales — you take no fire damage. Once per round, fly a near distance, then land. (+1 STR)
- **Minor** Dread gaze — once per scene. One foe that meets your eyes is Frightened. A CHA check ends it.
- **Weakness** Oath — lie, flee a fight, or leave an innocent, and you have disadvantage until you atone. (-1 CHA)

## Curupira

The trail behind you points the wrong way. Your hair is the torch.

- **Major** Wrong trail — you cannot be tracked. Anyone following your trail goes the wrong way. (+1 DEX)
- **Minor** Torch hair — light, near. You never need a torch.
- **Weakness** Forest-bound — with no plant or soil in the room, disadvantage on INT checks. (-1 CON)

## Dog Soldier

Pack first. Squirrels second. Thinking a distant third.

- **Major** Pack — +1 to hit a foe an ally is also fighting. You track by scent. (+1 STR)
- **Minor** Good boy — beasts start friendly unless you hurt them.
- **Weakness** Squirrel — fail an INT check and a thrown ball, a squirrel, or the word walk costs your next action. (-2 INT)

## Dullahead

You carry your head. You would like a spare.

- **Major** Detached head — once per scene, set your head down. You see through it, near, around one corner, until you pick it up. (+1 CHA)
- **Minor** Already dead — you need no air. You cannot be Diseased.
- **Weakness** Loose head — while your head is off you, you are Blinded. Healing heals you for half. (-1 CON)

## Firbolg

Big, gentle, and out of slots until someone hurts a tree.

- **Major** Gentle giant — +6 gear slots. You understand beasts and plants. (+2 STR, +6 slots)
- **Minor** Hidden step — once per scene, invisible until you attack, cast, or speak.
- **Weakness** Too kind — disadvantage on your first attack each fight against a foe that has not hurt nature or an ally. (-1 DEX)

## Fomorian

Strong enough to bend a door. Charming enough to lose the room.

- **Major** Monstrous strength — +1 damage. You breathe water. (+2 STR, +1 dmg)
- **Minor** Sea-born — you swim at full speed and see in murky water.
- **Weakness** Cursed charm — CHA can never rise above 10. (-2 CHA)

## Gargoyle

Stand still and you are architecture. Then you are not.

- **Major** Stone skin — +2 AC on a turn you have not moved. (+1 CON)
- **Minor** Statue — hold still and you pass as carved stone. No check, until you move.
- **Weakness** Bloodthirst — after you drop a foe, your next action is an attack on the nearest foe in reach. (-1 DEX)

## Glacial

Carved from ice. The joke did not survive the carving.

- **Major** Glacier — you take no cold damage. DR 1. (+2 CON, +1 dr)
- **Minor** Chill touch — once per scene, freeze one hinge, puddle, or lock solid.
- **Weakness** Meltwater — fire damage against you is doubled. (-2 CHA)

## Half Djinn

One wish, for someone else, and a foot of air under your shoes.

- **Major** Wish — once per scene, one other crawler rerolls and keeps the new roll. (+1 CHA)
- **Minor** Hover — you float a foot up. Rough ground, mud, and caltrops miss you.
- **Weakness** Bargains — break a promise and you lose Wish until the next floor. (-1 STR)

## High Goblin

Smarter than the goblins. They have noticed.

- **Major** Superior — advantage on INT checks about traps, machines, and what loot is worth. (+2 INT)
- **Minor** Darkvision — you see in the dark.
- **Weakness** Small and smug — goblins attack you first. Other people underestimate you. (-1 STR)

## Incubus/Sucubus

They want you. One drink and the floor wants you less.

- **Major** Towering charm — advantage on CHA checks to persuade, seduce, or lie. (+2 CHA)
- **Minor** Read desire — once per scene, you learn what one person you can see wants most.
- **Weakness** Lightweight — one drink and you are Drunk. Disadvantage on DEX checks for the scene. (-1 CON)

## Intellect Hunter

A worm in a body that is already going off.

- **Major** Body hopper — when your host dies, crawl into a fresh corpse or a helpless creature in reach and wear it. (+2 INT)
- **Minor** Host memories — when you enter a host, ask one question of its memory.
- **Weakness** Rotting host — lose 1 max HP each day in the same body. Out of a host you have 1 HP. (-2 CON)

## Kua-tin

The Syndicate's better. Dry land disagrees.

- **Major** Unmatched swimmer — swim at double speed. You breathe water. (+1 DEX)
- **Minor** Syndicate blood — Syndicate staff treat you as their better.
- **Weakness** Rebreather — out of water without one, you suffocate. (-1 CHA)

## Lego Minifig

One inch of plastic. The gap was made for you.

- **Major** Tiny — +2 AC. You fit through any gap. Nobody notices you unless you want them to. (+2 DEX, +2 ac)
- **Minor** Master Builder — once per rest, snap scrap into one simple tool or a short bridge.
- **Weakness** Plastic — STR can never rise above 8. You snap apart. You do not bleed. (-2 STR)

## Orc

Tusks, bristles, and no patience for a riddle.

- **Major** Tusked — +1 AC. Advantage against being shoved or knocked Prone. (+2 STR, +1 ac)
- **Minor** Bristled — cold weather and a weak poison do not bother you.
- **Weakness** Thick — disadvantage on INT checks to read, recall, or puzzle. (-1 INT)

## Red Squirrel

Too cute to hit. Too small to carry the loot.

- **Major** Too cute — the first attack against you each fight has disadvantage. (+2 DEX)
- **Minor** Climber — scale walls at full speed. Stash one small item in your cheeks.
- **Weakness** Tiny — your weapons deal one die smaller. -4 gear slots. (-2 STR, -4 slots)

## Rhineterra

A hallway, a straight line, and whoever was standing in it.

- **Major** Charge — move at least a near distance in a straight line and your melee attack deals +1 damage die. (+2 STR, +1 dmg_dice, when charge)
- **Minor** Thick hide — DR 1. (+1 dr)
- **Weakness** Can't turn — disadvantage on DEX checks to dodge, swerve, or stop short. (-1 DEX)

## The Chip

You left the meat behind. Healing did not get the memo.

- **Major** Mechanical — you cannot be Poisoned or Diseased. You need no food, sleep, or air. (+1 CON)
- **Minor** Interface — once per scene, plug into a machine and learn what it does.
- **Weakness** Machine — healing magic heals you for half. Lightning damage against you is doubled. (-1 CHA)

## Tuatha Dé Danann

Beautiful, brave, and allergic to the good armour.

- **Major** Ageless — advantage on checks against fear and charm. +1 to hit on your first attack each fight. (+1 CHA, +1 atk, when first attack)
- **Minor** Fair folk — strangers start friendly.
- **Weakness** Iron-sick — iron weapons deal +1 damage to you. You cannot wear iron armour. (-1 CON)

## Wolfman

The bite works. The off switch does not.

- **Major** Killing machine — bite and claw deal 1d8. +1 to hit while below half HP. (+2 STR, +1 atk, when below half HP)
- **Minor** Keen nose — track by scent. You smell fear on a liar.
- **Weakness** Blood up — when you take damage, pass a CON check or your next attack is on the nearest creature, friend or foe. (-1 INT)

_Source: `dungeons/global/races.yaml`._
